root_cause.text: XFS scrub/repair teardown paths unconditionally called xfarray/xfblob destroy routines on uninitialized or already-freed pointers in context structures, causing invalid frees during cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds pointer validity checks before every affected `xfarray_destroy`/`xfblob_destroy` call and explicitly nulls the fields afterward (e.g., `if (ragi->iunlink_prev) xfarray_destroy(ragi->iunlink_prev); ragi->iunlink_prev = NULL;`), and the CVE/commit message states “only call the xfarray and xfblob destructor if we have a valid pointer, and be sure to null out that pointer afterwards.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard AGI cleanup against null or stale xfarray pointers by checking before destroy and nulling the fields afterward.
intent_record.what: The cleanup function was changed to wrap both xfarray_destroy calls in null checks and then explicitly assign ragi->iunlink_prev and ragi->iunlink_next to NULL after destruction.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cleanup now safely handles cases where either array pointer was never allocated or may already be cleared, and it also resets the pointers after freeing to avoid leaving stale dangling references behind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add null checks before destroying xattr blob and record containers during teardown to make cleanup safe when those allocations were never created.
intent_record.what: The teardown function was changed to wrap the calls to xfblob_destroy(rx->xattr_blobs) and xfarray_destroy(rx->xattr_records) in null checks, so each destroy function is now only called if the corresponding pointer is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the teardown path from invoking destroy routines on possibly uninitialized or absent xattr_blobs and xattr_records pointers, avoiding potential null-pointer related crashes or invalid cleanup behavior during teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add NULL checks in directory repair teardown to safely destroy optional allocations and clear cleaned-up state.
intent_record.what: The teardown function was changed from unconditionally calling xfblob_destroy(rd->dir_names) and xfarray_destroy(rd->dir_entries) to first checking each pointer for non-NULL before destroying it, and then assigning rd->dir_names = NULL after each destroy block; the second NULL assignment appears to target rd->dir_names again instead of rd->dir_entries.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents destroy functions from being called on NULL pointers, reducing the risk of invalid teardown behavior if either allocation was never initialized. It also clears rd->dir_names after teardown to avoid leaving a stale pointer, though the duplicated assignment means rd->dir_entries is not cleared and may indicate an incomplete or mistaken cleanup change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add null checks and pointer clearing in dirtree buffer cleanup to make destruction safe for absent or previously cleaned resources.
intent_record.what: The cleanup function was changed to wrap xfblob_destroy(dl->path_names) and xfarray_destroy(dl->path_steps) in separate null checks, and to explicitly set dl->path_names and dl->path_steps to NULL after the conditional destroy calls.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents destroy routines from being called on null or already-cleared pointers and leaves the structure fields in a known null state after cleanup, reducing the risk of invalid destruction or accidental reuse during repeated or partial cleanup paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a NULL check before destroying xnc->nlinks during teardown to prevent invalid cleanup on an uninitialized or already cleared array.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to xfarray_destroy(xnc->nlinks) was changed to a conditional call guarded by if (xnc->nlinks), while keeping the subsequent assignment xnc->nlinks = NULL unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, teardown now only destroys the array when the nlinks pointer is non-NULL, preventing a destroy call on a NULL pointer and avoiding a possible crash or invalid cleanup path during teardown.

The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full setup and teardown paths for the new nlinks scrub state, including initialization in `xchk_nlinks_setup_scan` and cleanup in `xchk_nlinks_teardown_scan`.

The vulnerable construct is present: `xchk_nlinks_teardown_scan` unconditionally destroys state without checking whether it was ever initialized: `xfarray_destroy(xnc->nlinks);`, then `xchk_iscan_teardown(&xnc->collect_iscan);` and `mutex_destroy(&xnc->lock);`. There are no guards around `xnc->nlinks`, `collect_iscan`, or the mutex initialization state.

This is problematic because `xchk_nlinks_setup_scan` can fail partway through initialization and then jump to teardown: it does `xnc->sc = sc;`, `mutex_init(&xnc->lock);`, `xchk_iscan_start(sc, 30000, 100, &xnc->collect_iscan);`, and then `error = xfarray_create(..., &xnc->nlinks); if (error) goto out_teardown;`. If `xfarray_create` fails before assigning a valid array object, `out_teardown` calls `xchk_nlinks_teardown_scan(xnc)`, which still executes `xfarray_destroy(xnc->nlinks);` on whatever value is in `xnc->nlinks`.

The root cause says teardown paths unconditionally called xfarray/xfblob destroy routines on uninitialized or already-freed pointers in context structures. That exact pattern exists here because there is no prior `xnc->nlinks = NULL;` in `xchk_nlinks_setup_scan`, and the teardown assumes the pointer is valid enough to destroy. Although it sets `xnc->nlinks = NULL` after destroy, that only helps after a successful first cleanup; it does not prevent the initial invalid destroy on an uninitialized pointer.

The fix is not present because there are no initialization-state checks or NULL checks before destroy, and no defensive zeroing of `xnc->nlinks` before any fallible setup work.
